questions.text: Pedestrian means a road user on foot; a pedestrian is also
answers: a person pushing or pulling a hand truck with an overall width not exceeding 600 mm.
a driver of any non-motorised vehicle moving at a speed of less than 30 km.h-1.
a horse-drawn vehicle driver and a person pushing or pulling a hand truck with an overall length not exceeding 150 cm.

questions.text: Pedestrian means a road user on foot; a pedestrian is also a person who
answers: rides a bicycle, motorcycle or scooter with an auxiliary motor.
rides a bicycle or pushes a bicycle or motorcycle.
pushes a bicycle, motorcycle or scooter with an auxiliary motor.

questions.text: Pedestrian means a road user on foot; a pedestrian is also a person who
answers: moves on skis, skates, scooter without an auxiliary motor, skateboard or similar sports equipment.
rides a bicycle, motorcycle or scooter with an auxiliary motor.
moves at walking speed on a bicycle.

questions.text: Footway means
answers: only the road or part of the road marked with the appropriate traffic sign.
the right-hand shoulder; where there is no shoulder, footway means the right-hand edge of the carriageway one metre wide.
a road or part of a road intended for pedestrian use, usually separated from the carriageway by height or other means.

questions.text: Is the person pushing a motorcycle considered a driver?
answers: Only if he/she is wearing a motorcycle helmet properly fitted to his head.
Yes.
No.

questions.text: Shoulder means
answers: a place off the road where only the driver of a non-motorised vehicle may enter.
the part of the road reserved for the use of vehicles with a maximum permissible gross laden weight exceeding 3,500 kg.
the part of the road from the edge of the carriageway to the edge of the road.

questions.text: Motor vehicle means
answers: a rail and non-rail vehicle powered by its own engine.
a vehicle powered by its own engine, excluding motorcycle, tractor and motorised hand truck.
a non-rail vehicle powered by its own engine and a trolleybus.

questions.text: Non-restriction means the obligation
answers: of a passenger not to distract the driver`s attention by talking loudly, talking on the telephone, drinking or other similar activity.
of a driver not to disturb the driver of the vehicle being overtaken under any circumstances by giving an audible warning signal or a light warning signal.
of a road user to behave in such a way as not to obstruct another road user.

questions.text: Non-endangerment means the obligation of a road user
answers: not to go around or overtake a vehicle carrying dangerous goods and to drive behind such a vehicle at a distance of at least 50 m.
to behave in such a way as not to obstruct another road user in any way.
to act in such a way that no danger is caused to another road user.

questions.text: Road user means a person who
answers: is directly involved in road traffic.
drives a vehicle.
pushes or pulls a hand truck with an overall width not exceeding 600 mm.

questions.text: Driver means a person who
answers: drives only a motor vehicle.
pushes a motorcycle, moves on skis or roller skates, pulls or pushes a sledge.
drives a vehicle.

questions.text: Stopping means
answers: interrupting driving due to a fault on the vehicle that has rendered it inoperable.
bringing a vehicle to a standstill for a time exceeding five minutes.
bringing a vehicle to a standstill for the time strictly necessary for the expeditious embarkation or disembarkation of the persons carried or for the expeditious loading or unloading of the load.

questions.text: Stopping means
answers: interrupting the driving of a motor vehicle for a reason independent of the driver`s will.
only bringing a vehicle to a standstill that does not exceed three minutes.
bringing a vehicle to a standstill for the time strictly necessary for the expeditious embarkation or disembarkation of the persons carried or for the expeditious loading or unloading of the load.

questions.text: Vehicle stopping means
answers: interrupting the driving for a reason independent of the driver`s will.
bringing a vehicle to a standstill for the time strictly necessary for the expeditious embarkation or disembarkation of the persons carried or for the expeditious loading or unloading of the load.
bringing a motor vehicle to a standstill for the time strictly necessary for the expeditious embarkation or disembarkation of the persons carried, however, maximum for three minutes.

questions.text: Reduced visibility means
answers: visibility such that road users cannot see each other clearly enough, nor can they see objects on the road, especially from dusk to dawn, in fog, snow, rain and in tunnels.
visibility from 6 p.m. to 7 a.m. and from 1 July to 31 August only from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m.
visibility such that the driver of a motor vehicle cannot see other road users sufficiently clearly because of soiling or damage to the vehicle`s windscreens.

questions.text: Road user
answers: is not obliged to pay attention to light signals.
is obliged to pay attention to informative traffic signs and light signals; only a tram driver is obliged to pay attention to other traffic signs and traffic devices.

is obliged to behave in a disciplined and considerate manner so as not to endanger the safety or free flow of road traffic, whereby he is obliged to adapt his behaviour in particular to the construction, traffic-technical condition of the road, the situation in road traffic, weather conditions and his abilities.

questions.text: Road user
answers: is obliged to obey the instruction resulting from a traffic sign or traffic device.
is not obliged to pay attention to traffic devices.
is obliged to pay attention to regulatory traffic signs and light signals; only a motor vehicle driver is obliged to pay attention to other traffic signs and traffic devices.

questions.text: A road user is prohibited from using
answers: winter tyres between 15 November and 31 March.
audible warning signals.

technical means and devices, the operation of which makes it possible to detect or influence the functions of technical means used in the performance of tasks in the field of supervision of road traffic safety and free flow, or their location in the vehicle in a way that makes their use possible.

questions.text: A driver is obliged to
answers: secure the vehicle and the goods carried against theft by means fitted to the vehicle by its manufacturer if he moves away from the vehicle for more than 30 minutes.
use for driving only a vehicle that can be driven in road traffic.
stop the vehicle in front of a pedestrian crossing even if there are no pedestrians.

questions.text: A driver is obliged to
answers: fully concentrate on driving and monitor the traffic situation.
fully concentrate on driving; he is only obliged to monitor the traffic situation in certain special cases, in particular when driving at higher speeds or carrying dangerous goods.
monitor the traffic situation only when driving on the motorway, on the road for motor vehicles and on a class I road.

questions.text: A driver is obliged to
answers: have regard for a vehicle marked as a driving school training vehicle.
not have regard for a vehicle marked as a driving school training vehicle.
have regard for any vehicle travelling at a speed greater than 90 km.h-1.

questions.text: A driver is obliged to
answers: fully concentrate on driving; this does not apply in reduced visibility.
stop the vehicle in front of a pedestrian crossing only if there is a group of pedestrians on it.
take extra care with cyclists and pedestrians, especially children, people with disabilities, especially those using a white cane, and the elderly.

questions.text: A driver is obliged to take extra care with pedestrians, especially those using a white cane. Which road user uses a white cane?
answers: Persons with hearing impairment.
Persons with visual impairments (blind, partially sighted and visually impaired).
A policeman while directing traffic at a junction, which he holds in his right hand.

questions.text: A driver must not drive a motor vehicle for the duration of a penalty of prohibition of activity consisting in the prohibition to drive motor vehicles or for the duration of a sanction of prohibition of activity consisting in the prohibition to drive motor vehicles
answers: of a group at the discretion of the driver of the motor vehicle.
only of B group.
of any group.

questions.text: A driver must not consume alcohol or any other addictive substance
answers: at least 12 hours after he has finished driving.
while driving a vehicle.
only when driving a motorcycle and a vehicle with a maximum gross vehicle weight exceeding 3,500 kg.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
answers: may drive a motor vehicle at a time after having consumed alcohol or an addictive substance when alcohol or another addictive substance may still be present in his body, if the traffic situation permits, especially in reduced visibility.
may drive a motor vehicle for no more than 30 minutes after consuming alcohol.
must not drive a motor vehicle at a time after having consumed alcohol or another addictive substance when alcohol or another addictive substance may still be present in his body.

questions.text: A driver must not drive a vehicle after taking a medicine at a time when
answers: the medicine may impair his ability to drive; this does not apply if a doctor is a passenger.
he does not have the medicines he takes regularly and the phone number of his doctor with him.
the medicine may impair his ability to drive.

questions.text: A driver must not
answers: drive a vehicle on local roads between 1.00 a.m. and 5.00 a.m.
drive a vehicle after taking a medicine at a time when the medicine may impair his ability to drive.
drive a vehicle after taking a medicine at a time when the medicine may impair his ability to drive; this does not apply if there is a passenger in the vehicle.

questions.text: A driver must not hand over the driving of a vehicle to a person who
answers: meets the conditions laid down in the Road Traffic Act, but is under 23 years of age.
does not have at least three years` experience of driving such a vehicle.
does not meet the conditions for driving laid down in the Road Traffic Act.

questions.text: A driver must not hand over the driving of a vehicle to a person who
answers: does not have at least two years` experience of driving such a vehicle.
meets the conditions laid down in the Road Traffic Act, but is under 21 years of age.
is under the influence of alcohol or another addictive substance.

questions.text: A driver must not hand over the driving of a vehicle to a person
answers: who meets the conditions laid down in the Road Traffic Act, but is under 20 years of age.
whose ability to drive the vehicle is otherwise impaired, in particular by injury, illness, sickness or fatigue.
who does not have at least two years` experience of driving such a vehicle.

questions.text: A driver must not
answers: damage the environment, in particular by driving on public green spaces or roadside greenery.
stop and wait on a purpose built road in a municipality.
obstruct only faster moving regular public passenger transport vehicles by driving unreasonably slowly.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
answers: must not operate a telephone device while driving a vehicle, except by using a hands-free system.
must not listen to the radio while driving.
may operate a telephone device while driving a vehicle.

questions.text: A driver must not
answers: reduce the driving speed suddenly under any circumstances.
use derogatory gestures towards other road users.
stop on the left on a one-way road.

questions.text: A driver must not
answers: reduce the driving speed suddenly under any circumstances.
switch off the engine of a stationary vehicle when waiting for the “Go” light signal.
throw objects out of the vehicle and bother other road users or other persons by splashing puddles and mud.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle must not
answers: wait on a cycle crossing, but may stop on a pedestrian crossing.
wait on a pedestrian crossing, but may stop on a cycle crossing.
stop the vehicle on a pedestrian crossing, a place for pedestrians to cross or a cycle crossing, unless road safety requires it.

questions.text: A driver may use a motor vehicle only on the road; this shall not apply if the motor vehicle is used in accordance with special regulations
answers: for transport to a residential or recreational facility.
with the consent of the passenger.
with the consent of the vehicle operator.

questions.text: If a driver discovers during the journey that the vehicle, load or load fixing does not comply with the conditions laid down,
answers: he is obliged to give a light warning signal by switching on the warning function of the direction indicator lamps.
he may continue driving to the nearest petrol station.
he is obliged to rectify the fault on the spot; if he is unable to do so, he may continue driving at a reasonable speed only to the nearest place where the fault can be rectified.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle which is compulsorily fitted with safety clothing is obliged to wear the safety clothing when he is
answers: in a car park in reduced visibility.
on the carriageway outside the vehicle during an emergency stop, especially if the journey is interrupted due to a fault in the vehicle or as a result of an accident.
at a petrol station.

questions.text: If the driver of a motor vehicle which is compulsorily fitted with safety clothing is on the carriageway outside the vehicle during an emergency stop, especially if the journey is interrupted due to a fault in the vehicle or as a result of an accident, he is obliged
answers: to have the safety clothing on.
to place a non-dazzling white light 20 m behind the vehicle.
to call a towing service immediately.

questions.text: The operator of a vehicle must not entrust the driving of the vehicle to a person who
answers: does not meet the conditions for driving it laid down by the Road Traffic Act or a special regulation.
is under 25 years of age, even if he fulfils the conditions laid down.
does not have at least two years` experience in driving a motor vehicle.

questions.text: The operator must not entrust the driving of the vehicle to a person
answers: who is under 25 years of age, even if he otherwise fulfils the conditions laid down.
whose identity he does not know.
who does not have at least two years` experience in driving a motor vehicle.

questions.text: If a vehicle, including the load or load fixing, does not comply with the conditions laid down, the operator of the vehicle
answers: may order the vehicle to be used for driving in the municipality.
must not order or allow the vehicle to be used for driving.
may, with the consent of the driver, allow the vehicle to be used for driving.

questions.text: The operator of a vehicle is obliged to ensure that the necessary number of competent and properly instructed persons are taken on the journey if he knows in advance that
answers: dangerous goods or live animals will be carried in the vehicle.
the driver does not have the necessary driving skills.
road safety will require it.

questions.text: The operator of a vehicle is obliged to ensure that the colour design and markings of the vehicle cannot be confused with the colour design and markings of the vehicles
answers: of the Police Force, Military Police, Prison and Court Guard Service, municipal police, Fire and Rescue Corps or other fire-fighting units.
intended for chairpersons of higher territorial units.
foreign representative offices established in the territory of the Slovak Republic.

questions.text: A person seated in a seat compulsorily fitted with a safety belt or other restraint device
answers: is obliged to use this device only when driving at speeds exceeding 40 km/h.
is obliged to use the device when driving outside a municipality.
is obliged to use the device.

questions.text: A person seated in a seat compulsorily fitted with a safety belt or other restraint device is obliged to use the device; this does not apply to
answers: a person with a body height of less than 130 cm.
a person with a body height of less than 150 cm, with the exception of a person who is obliged to use a restraint device under the conditions laid down in a special regulation.
a person with a body height of less than 150 cm, who is not obliged to use a restraint device under the conditions laid down in a special regulation.

questions.text: A person seated in a seat compulsorily fitted with a safety belt or other restraint device is obliged to use the device; this does not apply to
answers: a person who cannot be restrained for medical reasons; such a person must produce a certificate of exemption from the use of vehicle restraint systems.
a driver while driving in a municipality.
a passenger sitting in the back seat of the vehicle.

questions.text: A child with a body height of less than 150 cm when transported in a vehicle equipped with a safety system must be
answers: restrained by a safety belt in the front seat only.
clamped by a child restraint that is suitable for the child`s physical constitution.
restrained by a safety belt outside a municipality.

questions.text: A seat in a vehicle which is not equipped with a safety system must not be used to carry
answers: children aged four years and over with a body height of less than 150 cm.
any persons.
children up to the age of three years.

questions.text: A front seat in a vehicle which is not equipped with a safety system must not be used to carry children
answers: up to the age of three years.
aged three years and over with a body height of less than 150 cm.
with a body height of less than 120 cm.

questions.text: A child aged three years and over with a body height of less than 150 cm
answers: must not be carried in the front seat in a vehicle which is not equipped with a safety system.
may be carried in the front seat in a vehicle only outside a municipality.
may be carried in the front seat in a vehicle only in a municipality.

questions.text: A child restraint must not be rearward-facing (rearward-facing is turning in the opposite direction to the direction of travel) in a seat that is
answers: protected by a frontal airbag, unless the airbag has been disabled or automatically deactivated.
equipped with a three-point safety belt.
protected by a frontal airbag and the airbag has not been deactivated.

questions.text: If vehicles of categories M1 and N1 are not fitted with a child restraint,
answers: a child under the age of three can be restrained in the rear seat of the car with a safety belt when being transported.
it is not possible to carry a child with a body height of less than 150 cm in such a vehicle.
a child aged three or over can be restrained in the rear seat of the vehicle with a safety belt fitted to the vehicle when being transported in a municipality.

questions.text: The driver is obliged to drive on the carriageway or in the lane
answers: on the left at the left-hand edge of the carriageway or lane.
on the right, on the right-hand shoulder.
on the right at the right-hand edge of the carriageway or lane.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle may enter the shoulder
answers: when making a U-turn and reversing.
whenever necessary to carry out any driving action.
only when stopping and waiting or when passing and avoiding a traffic obstacle.

questions.text: The driver of a motor vehicle, when entering a shoulder, is obliged to
answers: take care to pay extra attention.
stop the vehicle.
give a warning signal.

questions.text: Outside a municipality on a road with two or more lanes marked on the carriageway in one direction of travel, vehicles shall be driven
answers: in any lane.
in the right-hand lane; the other lanes may be used if necessary for passing, overtaking, making a U-turn or turning.
in the left-hand lane; only the driver of a non-motorised vehicle may use the other lanes.

questions.text: In a municipality on a road with two or more lanes marked on the carriageway in one direction of travel, the driver of a vehicle may use to drive
answers: the left-hand lane only; only the driver of a non-motorised vehicle may use the other lanes.
the right-hand lane only; the other lanes may only be used for overtaking or turning.
any lane.

questions.text: In a municipality on a road with two or more lanes marked on the carriageway in one direction of travel, the driver of a passenger car may use to drive
answers: any lane.
the left-hand lane only; only the driver of a non-motorised vehicle may use the other lanes.
the right-hand lane only; the other lanes may only be used for overtaking or turning.

questions.text: Vehicles can drive parallel to each other
answers: only if they are driving on a motorway and on a road for motor vehicles.

where traffic is so dense on a road with two or more lanes in one direction of travel that continuous streams of vehicles are formed in which the driver of a motor vehicle can drive only at a speed which depends on the speed of the vehicles in front of him.
only if they are driving on a one-way road with two lanes in the municipality.

questions.text: If vehicles driving in a municipality in all lanes at the same time would obstruct a faster moving vehicle, a driver who is driving in
answers: the left-hand lane is obliged to stop the vehicle immediately.
the right-hand lane is obliged to vacate it as soon as possible.
the left-hand lane is obliged to vacate it as soon as possible; this does not apply if the driver uses the left-hand lane for passing, turning, making a U-turn or overtaking.

questions.text: A driver crossing from one lane to another lane
answers: may endanger a driver driving in the lane into which he is crossing.
may signal a change of direction if the road safety or free flow of traffic so requires.
is obliged to signal a change of direction.

questions.text: Where two lanes converge into a single lane in such a way that it is not obvious which is the through lane, the driver in the left-hand lane must give way to the driver in the right-hand lane, but this does not apply
answers: if the driver in the left-hand lane is driving a lorry with a maximum permissible gross laden weight exceeding 3,500 kg.
if the driver in the left-hand lane is driving a special motor vehicle.

in parallel driving, where the driver driving in the right-hand lane is obliged to allow the driver of the first vehicle in the left-hand lane to merge into the column of moving vehicles if the latter signals a change of direction to the right.

questions.text: If there is a traffic obstacle in a lane when driving in parallel, the driver of a vehicle in the clear lane must allow
answers: the drivers of all vehicles in the lane in which the obstacle is located to pass the obstacle.
the driver of the first vehicle in the lane in which the obstacle is located to pass the obstacle if the driver signals a change of direction.
only drivers of regular public passenger transport vehicles to pass the obstacle.

questions.text: If, when driving in parallel, the driver of a vehicle in the clear lane allows the driver of the first vehicle in the lane in which the obstacle is located to pass the obstacle, the driver passing the obstacle must not
answers: signal a change of direction.
under any circumstances drive at a speed of more than 15 km/h.
endanger the driver driving in the clear lane.

questions.text: In the event of a traffic density which gives rise to a column of stationary vehicles on a motorway or on a directionally divided road outside a municipality with at least two lanes in one direction of travel, a driver of the vehicle is obliged to
answers: immediately stop the vehicle.
perform such a driving action as to enable a rescue lane to be formed in the centre between two lanes of traffic when driving in parallel.
perform such a driving action as to enable a rescue lane to be formed in the centre between two lanes of traffic if the free flow of road traffic requires it.

questions.text: When forming a rescue lane, a driver of the vehicle, for the time strictly necessary,
answers: is not entitled to enter places where it is otherwise prohibited, provided that this does not endanger another road user.
is entitled to enter places where it is otherwise prohibited, provided that this does not restrict another road user.
is entitled to enter places where it is otherwise prohibited, provided that this does not endanger another road user.

questions.text: The rescue lane can be used by
answers: a driver of any vehicle.
a driver of a regular public passenger transport bus.
a driver of a vehicle with the right of way.

questions.text: The rescue lane can be used by
answers: a tractor driver.
a driver of a regular public passenger transport bus.
a driver of a vehicle ensuring that the consequences of a traffic accident are eliminated.

questions.text: The use of the rescue lane by a driver of a vehicle other than a vehicle with the right of way or a vehicle ensuring that the consequences of a traffic accident are eliminated is
answers: permitted if this is required by the free flow of road traffic.
permitted if he does not endanger other road users.
prohibited.

questions.text: Along the boarding islands or safety zones, drivers drive
answers: on the right; driving on the left is only permitted if driving on the right is obstructed by an obstacle or if it is safer to do so in view of the dimensions of the vehicle or load.
on the left under any circumstances.
on the left; driving on the right is only permitted if driving on the left is obstructed by an obstacle.

questions.text: Along a tram, drivers drive
answers: on the left unless a traffic sign permits driving on the right.
on the left under any circumstances.
on the right unless a traffic sign permits driving on the left.

questions.text: It is permitted to enter the tram track at the level of the carriageway
answers: under any circumstances.
only when passing, turning and overtaking.
only when passing, turning, making a U-turn, entering the road, or if this is permitted by a traffic sign or if exceptional circumstances require it.

questions.text: A tram track which is raised above or lowered below the level of the carriageway, or which is otherwise separated from the carriageway, in particular by a kerb, may be crossed
answers: at any place, unless there is a tram nearby.
only transversely, and at a place adapted for that purpose.
at any place, and always transversely.

questions.text: When entering and crossing a tram track raised above the level of the carriageway, the driver
answers: may obstruct the tram in running only to the extent necessary for the performance of the driving operation.
must not endanger or restrict the tram in running.
may, depending on the circumstances, restrict the tram in running, but must not endanger it.

questions.text: If the tram is travelling at a different speed to other vehicles travelling in the same direction
answers: it means mutual overtaking if the tram runs slower than other vehicles.
it does not mean mutual overtaking.
it means mutual overtaking.

questions.text: If a vehicle in a dedicated lane is travelling at a different speed from other vehicles travelling in the same direction
answers: it means mutual overtaking if other vehicles are driving faster.
it does not mean mutual overtaking.
it means mutual overtaking.

questions.text: A properly marked taxi vehicle travelling in a dedicated bus or trolleybus lane
answers: may impede the free flow of traffic of the vehicles for which the dedicated lane is intended only when driving in non-reduced visibility.
must not impede the free flow of traffic of the vehicles for which the dedicated lane is intended.
may impede the free flow of traffic of the vehicles for which the dedicated lane is intended.

questions.text: A driver who has stopped a vehicle behind a regular public passenger transport vehicle which has stopped in a municipality at a stop without a boarding island or without a platform on a raised tram track may continue driving if
answers: the driver of a regular public passenger transport vehicle signals to him.
he does not endanger a person boarding or getting out of a regular public passenger transport vehicle.
he does not endanger or restrict a person boarding or getting out of a regular public passenger transport vehicle.

questions.text: The driver in the section of the stop of vehicles of regular public passenger transport is obliged to
answers: take extra care and drive at an appropriate speed so as not to endanger or restrict a person getting out of or into a regular public passenger transport vehicle.
take extra care and drive at an appropriate speed so as not to endanger a person getting out of or into a regular public passenger transport vehicle.
switch on the device enabling the warning function of the direction indicator lamps.

questions.text: A driver who deviates from the direction of travel when passing a stopped or stationary vehicle, a traffic obstacle or a pedestrian
answers: is not obliged to signal a change of direction.
must not endanger or restrict the driver of an oncoming vehicle.
must not restrict the following driver.

questions.text: A driver who deviates from the direction of travel when passing a stopped or stationary vehicle, a traffic obstacle or a pedestrian
answers: may endanger another road user.
must not endanger or restrict the following driver or any other road user.
must not endanger the following driver or any other road user.

questions.text: A driver of a vehicle who deviates from the direction of travel when passing a stopped or stationary vehicle
answers: may restrict oncoming drivers.
has the right of way.
is obliged to signal a change of direction.

questions.text: When passing a stationary regular public passenger transport vehicle, the driver must take into account the possibility of persons running onto the carriageway and
answers: for this purpose always drive at a speed no faster than 15 km/h.
adjust his driving so that they are not endangered.
for this purpose always stop the vehicle.

questions.text: When passing a stationary regular public passenger transport vehicle, the driver must take into account the possibility of persons running onto the carriageway and adjust his driving so that they are not endangered; this
answers: does not apply to the driver of an oncoming vehicle.
also applies to the driver of an oncoming vehicle.
does not apply to the driver of a motorcycle and the driver of a non-motorised vehicle.

questions.text: Overtaking is carried out
answers: on the left; a vehicle changing direction to the left is overtaken on the right when there is no longer any doubt as to its next direction of travel.
on the right; only a motorcycle is overtaken on the left.
on the left under any circumstances.

questions.text: When driving in a merging or diverging lane
answers: the speed of vehicle must not be higher than that of vehicles in the through lane.
a vehicle travelling in the through lane may also be overtaken on the right.
a vehicle travelling in the through lane may not be overtaken on the right.

questions.text: A driver who deviates from the direction of travel when overtaking
answers: is obliged to signal a change of direction.
is obliged to give a light warning signal in the municipality.
may endanger the drivers following him only to a small extent.

questions.text: A driver who deviates from the direction of travel when overtaking
answers: may endanger the following drivers.
must not endanger the following drivers.
may endanger the following drivers if he drives at a speed greater than 60 km/h.

questions.text: When overtaking, a driver must not endanger or restrict the drivers of the vehicles in front of which he is merging after overtaking while being obliged to
answers: signal a change of direction.
not signal a change of direction in reduced visibility.
give an audible warning signal in the municipality to alert the driver of the vehicle being overtaken.

questions.text: When overtaking, the driver must maintain sufficient lateral distance from the vehicle being overtaken
answers: and while doing so, he is not obliged to take into account the weather conditions and the condition of the carriageway.
and while doing so, he must take into account in particular the speed, the type of his vehicle and the vehicle being overtaken, the weather conditions and the condition and nature of the carriageway.
and while doing so, he is not obliged to take into account the speed of the vehicle being overtaken.

questions.text: The driver of the vehicle being overtaken must not
answers: prevent overtaking in any way apart from increasing the speed of the vehicle.
increase the driving speed or otherwise prevent overtaking.
decrease the driving speed.

questions.text: A driver must not overtake if
answers: if a special motor vehicle is driving in front of him.
he did not warn the driver of the vehicle being overtaken in the municipality with an audible warning signal.
he could not safely get in front of the vehicle or vehicles he wishes to overtake.

questions.text: A driver must not overtake if he would
answers: have to increase his speed.
restrict the following vehicle or another road user.
endanger or restrict an oncoming driver, endanger another road user.

questions.text: A driver must not overtake if the driver of the vehicle ahead of him is signalling a change of direction
answers: to the left and cannot be overtaken on the right.
to the right.
to the left, under any circumstances.

questions.text: A driver must not overtake
answers: a non-motorised vehicle at a junction.

across a merging or diverging lane; this does not apply when overtaking a vehicle on the right which is changing direction to the left and where there is no longer any doubt about its next direction of travel.
if the driver of the vehicle in front signals a change of direction to the right in order to stop.

questions.text: A driver must not overtake...
answers: on the right, under any circumstances.
in the section 300 m before a junction.
on the shoulder; this does not apply when overtaking a vehicle on the right which is changing direction to the left and where there is no longer any doubt about its next direction of travel.

questions.text: A driver overtaking on the shoulder a vehicle on the right which is changing direction to the left, where there is no longer any doubt about its next direction of travel,
answers: must not stop.
must not endanger or restrict a pedestrian walking on the shoulder and a cyclist or the driver of a small motorcycle riding on the shoulder.
must not endanger a cyclist or the driver of a small motorcycle riding on the shoulder or restrict a pedestrian walking on the shoulder.
